title: Prime Density in Short Intervals (Bertrand to BHP)

problemStatement.formal: bertrand_density_lower_bound : ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → Nat.primeCounting n ≥ Nat.log 2 n
problemStatement.plain: How many primes are in a short interval [x, x+h]? This file formalizes the hierarchy from Bertrand's Postulate (1 prime in (n, 2n]) through Baker-Harman-Pintz 2001 (prime in [x, x+x^0.525]), up to the open Cramér and Legendre conjectures.
whyMatters: Connects Bertrand's classical result to modern short-interval prime density bounds
Gives concrete lower bound π(n) ≥ log₂(n) via iterated Bertrand doubling
Documents the frontier: BHP θ=0.525 proved, θ→0 (logarithmic gaps) open

proven: bertrand_iterated: π(2^k * n) ≥ π(n) + k for n ≥ 1
prime_density_summary: conjunction of all proved bounds
open: cramer_conjecture: max gap near p_n is O((log p_n)²) — axiomatized

currentState.focus: 12 theorems, 0 sorries, 3 axioms (BHP, Cramér, Legendre — open conjectures).

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Proved Bertrand-derived density bounds and documented BHP, Cramér, Legendre hierarchy.
builtItems: primeCountInInterval def: π(hi) - π(lo) as natural number
bertrand_density_lower_bound: induction using Nat.log 2 and Bertrand iteration
prime_gap_conjecture_bhp: follows from axiom bhp_short_interval via density calculation
insights: PrimeGapBounds.lean provides the key inductive lemma primeCounting_pow_two_mul
BHP (Baker-Harman-Pintz 2001) axiomatized as bhp_short_interval — deep sieve theory, not in Mathlib
Cramér and Legendre conjectures are open — appropriately axiomatized
π(n) ≥ log₂(n) proved by iterating Bertrand: each doubling adds ≥1 prime

papers: Baker, R.C., Harman, G., Pintz, J. (2001). The difference between consecutive primes, II. Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society
